claim: With the Object Ownership setting Object writer, the AWS account that uploads an object owns the object, has full control over it and can grant other users access to it through ACLs: when another account uploads an object to your general purpose bucket, that account (the object writer) owns the object. Object Ownership can be set so that ACLs are disabled and you, as the bucket owner, automatically own every object in the bucket.

qualifiers.condition: Object Ownership set to Object writer

evidence.quote: By default, when another AWS account uploads an object to your S3 general purpose bucket, that account (the object writer) owns the object, has access to it, and can grant other users access to it through access control lists (ACLs). You can use Object Ownership to change this default behavior so that ACLs are disabled and you, as the bucket owner, automatically own every object in your general purpose bucket.
**Object writer** – The AWS account that uploads an object owns the object, has full control over it, and can grant other users access to it through ACLs.
